research_cycles.hypothesis: The robust-domain PA-BPE candidate loses its fairness advantage relative to Classical BPE on a genuinely unseen literary work.
research_cycles.interpretation: The predicted universal fairness loss was not observed: robust_domain improves balance on Poe but is worse on Alice and pays a cost penalty. With one work per split this is descriptive evidence only; the earlier row-offset Books conclusion is not stable under correct work isolation.

research_cycles.reason: Tested the active cross-domain robustness hypothesis on native whole-work-separated Books data and retained the non-dominating, mixed result.
research_cycles.result: On Alice development, robust_domain Gini was 0.013865 versus Classical 0.002063. On Poe confirmation, robust_domain Gini was lower, 0.003492 versus 0.007505, but its worst-language cost was 61.708 versus 61.477 and total language-mean cost was 122.561 versus 121.136.
